english.title: Racially / religiously aggravated stalking without fear / alarm / distress
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) pursued a course of conduct which amounted to the stalking of **(..SPECIFY PERSON OR PERSONS..) and which you knew or ought to have known amounted to the harassment of

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_
(C)_[them]_

in that **(..SPECIFY THE DATES, PLACES AND NATURE OF CONDUCT..) and the offence was

(D)_[racially]_
(E)_[religiously]_

aggravated within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 32(1)(a) and (3) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 and section 2A of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
pursued a course of conduct in breach of section 1(1) of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997
that amounted to stalking
which you knew / ought to have known
amounted to harassment
and the offence was racially / religiously aggravated
within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For the non-racially / religiously aggravated version of this offence, see document H10641.
(ii) Where both, racial and religious hostility are involved, two offences should be charged.
(iii) If on trial on indictment, the jury find the suspect not guilty of the offence charged, they may find him guilty of the basic offence in section 2A of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997. The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is not available in the magistrates' court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence. This is also good practice in the Crown court.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction increased from 2nd May 2022, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003. This applies only to offences committed on or after that date, see section 282(4). For offences committed before 2nd May 2022 the maximum penalty on summary conviction is six months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
